relationships.subject: PGF2alpha
relationships.evidence_quote: Participants with dysmenorrhea had higher PGF2α (4.5 [1.6, 8.9] ng/mL, p = 0.014) than controls (1.1 [0.07, 4.4] ng/mL).

relationships.subject: COX-2
relationships.evidence_quote: It has been hypothesised that increased uterine cyclooxygenase‐2 activity increases prostaglandin synthesis, which increases uterine contractility, resulting in menstrual pain

relationships.subject: NSAIDs
relationships.evidence_quote: Although NSAIDs which target COX‐2 are the first‐line treatment for menstrual pain

key_findings: Menstrual effluent PGF2alpha was higher in adolescents with dysmenorrhea and modestly correlated with pain (r=0.37); PGE2 difference was not significant
NSAID users unexpectedly had higher PGF2alpha; LTB4, 15-HETE, 14,15-EET also elevated suggesting pathways beyond prostaglandins
